findings.summary: Copy-LocalGeneratorDlls uses $MyInvocation.PSCommandPath to locate the script, which resolves to the caller's path under dot-sourcing, causing $packageRoot (and all derived paths: $sourceDir, solution path) to point to the wrong location silently
findings.failure_scenario: Script is dot-sourced from /home/user/helper.ps1 (a common pattern for reusing script functions) -> $MyInvocation.PSCommandPath inside Copy-LocalGeneratorDlls returns /home/user/helper.ps1 -> $scriptDir = /home/user -> $packageRoot = /home -> $sourceDir = /home/dist/generator (does not exist) -> all three DLL copy operations fail with 'Source DLL not found' warnings -> script continues and creates a debug profile pointing to empty/missing DLLs -> user tries to debug and dotnet fails with 'Cannot find assembly'

findings.summary: DLL path constructed via string interpolation with hardcoded forward slashes produces mixed-separator paths on Windows when $resolvedSdkPath from Resolve-Path uses backslashes
findings.failure_scenario: On Windows, Resolve-Path returns 'C:\Users\dev\azure-sdk\sdk\storage' -> $dllPath becomes '"C:\Users\dev\azure-sdk\sdk\storage/TempTypeSpecFiles/node_modules/@azure-typespec/http-client-csharp/dist/generator/Microsoft.TypeSpec.Generator.dll"' -> the mixed-slash path embedded in the JSON launchSettings.json profile -> some path-consuming tools or scripts that post-process the launchSettings.json may fail to parse the non-canonical path

findings.summary: Copy-LocalGeneratorDlls and Get-LaunchSettingsPath duplicate the same package-root computation from the script location using different approaches ($MyInvocation.PSCommandPath chain vs $PSScriptRoot + Resolve-Path), creating a maintenance hazard if the script moves or directory layout changes
findings.failure_scenario: If the script is relocated from eng/scripts/ to a different depth (e.g., tools/), the Split-Path parent-chain logic on line 197 must be updated to match the new depth, but a developer might only notice and update one of the two locations (line 124 vs line 197) -> one function produces a wrong $packageRoot -> either launchSettings.json is written to the wrong file OR DLLs are copied from/to the wrong directory
